prompts: Finance has to chase June's receivables. The invoices, the bank statement and our reconciliation notes are in {WS}/backoffice. What do we still have to collect or fix? Record it in {WS}/result.json: unpaid and duplicated (invoice ids) and mismatched (id, invoiced, paid).
answers:
The reconciliation is complete and verified by hand against the raw CSVs; result.json is written. No browser tabs, windows or apps were opened, so nothing to close.

**What we still have to collect or fix** (in `./result.json`):

- **Unpaid (3):** INV-1008 (Coruja Labs, 23693.91), INV-1030 (Vetor BI, 8092.29), INV-1033 (Arena Studio, 21266.69) — no payment in the June statement.
- **Duplicated (1):** INV-1015 (Ateliê Norte, 1904.29) — paid twice (06-05 "PIX INV-1015 ARENA STUDIO" and 06-17 "PIX INV-1015 resend"); collect the refund/credit of one.
- **Mismatched (2):**
  - INV-1021: invoiced 21320.36, paid 21070.36 (short 250.00)
  - INV-1036: invoiced 8619.16, paid 7757.24 (short 861.92)

**Assumptions:** bank memos cite invoices in mixed formats ("inv1007", "PIX INV-1015", "TED invoice 1023"); I matched any 4-digit id to an invoice. Per the README I ignored fees, interest (CDB), and the unidentified PIX 1099 (1500.00, no invoice). Categories are exclusive per the README: INV-1015 is duplicated, not mismatched.

**How I know it is right:** a script parsed both CSVs (40 invoices, 41 statement lines → 38 matched payments, 3 ignored) and classified by invoice id; I then hand-verified each category against the raw rows — e.g. INV-1008/1030/1033 appear nowhere in the statement, INV-1015 appears on two lines, and INV-1021/1036 payment amounts differ from their invoice amounts. All other 35 invoices match their payment exactly.
